chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There was a woman from the Ansar who loved us, the Ahl al-Bayt, and frequently renewed her allegiance to us. Umar ibn al-Khattab met her one day while she was on her way to us. He said to her, "Where are you going, O old woman of the Ansar?" She said, "I am going to the Progeny of Muhammad to greet them, renew my covenant with them, and pay their rights."'

So Umar said to her, "Woe to you! There is no right for them today, neither from you nor from us. Their right was only during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). As for today, there is no right for them, so go back." So she went back until she came to Umm Salama. Umm Salama said to her, "What delayed you from coming to us?"

She said, "I met Umar ibn al-Khattab," and she informed her of what she had said to Umar and what Umar had said to her. Umm Salama said to her, "He lied. The right of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) remains obligatory upon the Muslims until the Day of Judgment."

key_terms.عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Era of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What did Umar ibn al-Khattab say about the rights of the Ahl al-Bayt after the Prophet's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the theological dispute between Umar ibn al-Khattab and Umm Salama regarding the enduring status of the Ahl al-Bayt. While Umar argued that the specific rights of the Prophet's family ceased with his death, Umm Salama affirmed their perpetual obligation upon the Muslim community, a view central to Shia jurisprudence. The narrative underscores the continuity of the Prophet's familial authority and the recognition of their rights as a lasting divine decree.
